Cardio-epic v0.2.2 second-honesty-patch + CCL-046 + CHK-5.13 (April 29, 2026, same-day afternoon after v0.2.1 morning patch)

Phase A acquisition for the canonical-document-named "Konigsberg 2023" atlas began per v0.2.1's revised critical path; web verification of the cited DOI (10.1093/nargab/lqad061) found two factual errors in PIPELINE_REFERENCE Part 2.4.

Error 1 — author attribution wrong. The actual paper at the cited DOI is Cuadrat, Kratzer, Giral Arnal, Rathgeber, Wreczycka, Blume, Gündüz, Ebenal, Mauno, Osberg, Moobed, Hartung, Jakobs, Seppelt, Meteva, Haghikia, Leistner, Landmesser, Akalin (2023) — NAR Genomics and Bioinformatics 5(2):lqad061, "Cardiovascular disease biomarkers derived from circulating cell-free DNA methylation." No "Konigsberg" appears in the author list. A second targeted search for any Konigsberg-authored cardiovascular methylation atlas paper returned zero hits.

Error 2 — cell-type content wrong. The canonical document claimed the atlas was a "28-cell-type extended atlas including sorted cardiomyocytes, cardiac fibroblasts, vascular endothelial, smooth muscle." The actual Cuadrat 2023 atlas is the Moss 2018 25-tissue base extended with three bulk ENCODE EPIC heart tissues: right atrium auricular (n=2 ENCODE accessions ENCSR517JQA + ENCSR280LMY), heart left ventricle (n=2 ENCSR515ZCU + ENCSR190PQG), coronary artery (n=2 ENCSR688OHW + ENCSR582BMR). 28 total tissues by adding three bulk heart regions to the Moss 25-tissue base, NOT 28 sorted cell types.

CCL-046 LL-CANONICAL-DOC-FACTUAL-ERROR. DISC-CARDIO-007 + CHK-5.12 (added in v0.2.1) protected against picking the wrong atlas from atlas_vault by forcing atlas selection to trace to the canonical document. But CHK-5.12 does not protect against following an incorrect citation in the canonical document itself. The Part 2.4 error sat undetected through cardio-epic v0.1 + v0.2 + v0.2.1 (three card versions) and only surfaced when CHK-5.12 forced the Phase A acquisition attempt.

CHK-5.13 documents-of-record citation-verification gate (added 2026-04-29 to TESTING_CHECKLIST.md). Companion to CHK-5.11 atlas-family-fitness and CHK-5.12 atlas-canonical-source-check. Before sealing a card publish or a card promotion, every external citation introduced in the new card content must have at least one web-verification pass: the DOI loads, the authors match the citation, the described content matches the abstract/methods/figures of the actual paper, every cohort accession resolves to an actual deposit. Cheap (one web search per citation) and catches an entire class of compounding errors. Generalizes to every external reference in cookbook documents.

"Cannot be deployed" framing dropped. The v0.2.1 deployment story said "Without this atlas, cardio-epic cannot be deployed" — anchored on a fictional sorted-cardiomyocyte atlas. With the anchor gone, the honest cardio-epic deployment story reads: cardio-epic is operational at v0.2 under the layered Moss+Loyfer atlas with Stage 1 immune as the validated workhorse (VAL-110 d=+1.08 normal vs BAV on aortic tissue). Cuadrat 2023 + Caggiano CelFiE TIM + EpiSCORE pan-tissue + Tanaka 2025 are integration ENHANCEMENTS that broaden cardio Stage 2 cell-of-origin coverage at bulk-heart-tissue resolution but do not gate deployment.

Sorted-cardiomyocyte array-CpG atlas — open published-literature gap. As of 2026-04-29 no such atlas exists at array-CpG resolution. Published cardiac methylation work covers either targeted CpG biomarkers (Zemmour 2018 FAM101A; Yamazoe 2021 mt-cfDNA), bulk heart tissues (Moss 2018 Left_atrium; Cuadrat 2023 right atrium + left ventricle + coronary artery), or sorted vascular cells (Loyfer 2023 vascular_endothelial + smooth_muscle as part of the layered atlas already in production). When published, sorted-cardiomyocyte array-CpG becomes a v1.0+ candidate. Cookbook surveillance pass for this atlas added to monthly atlas-surveillance routine.

v0.3 critical path revised: Cuadrat 2023 first (the actual paper at the DOI Part 2.4 cited; open access CC-BY, MIT-licensed R package deconvR, signature matrix in supplementary data, 6 ENCODE EPIC IDAT accessions); Caggiano CelFiE TIM cardiac second (HM450 manifest blocker); Tanaka 2025 third (nanopore→array bridge); EpiSCORE pan-tissue fourth (rpy2 integration).

VAL-112 + VAL-113 corrects this for cardio-epic v0.3.

Phase A engineering. Layered Moss+Loyfer reference_atlas.csv deduplicated from 7,890 rows to 6,105 unique CpGs (1,785 identical-value duplicate rows removed per CCL-047 LL-ATLAS-DEDUPE). Original preserved as reference_atlas_v0.2_with_duplicates.csv for audit-trail. Caggiano CelFiE TIM array-bridged atlas built: 1,581 WGBS regions → 254 unique array CpGs × 19 cell types via HM450 hg19 manifest CpG-in-region intersection. CHK-3.1C passed.

Phase B calibration on TCGA HM450 sesame Level 3 adjacent-normal n=210 (KIRC n=160 + PRAD n=50; same cohort that anchored VAL-106/107):

Phase C run-everything execution. All three atlases scored against all three cardio cohorts: GSE69138 stroke etiology (n=589), GSE84395 PAH variants (n=39), GSE84274 ascending aortic (n=24). 31,948 calibrated A-score readings sealed.

Findings under run-everything.

GSE84395 PAH — convergent strong cardiac signal across 3 atlases. Caggiano heart = +1.42 control vs iPAH (STRONGEST single-tile signal of any atlas tested); EpiSCORE HeartRef CM = −0.80 control vs iPAH; Loyfer Vascular_endothelial_cells = +0.83 control vs hPAH. Three independent atlases, three different cardiac references, three convergent positive findings. PAH detection is the most robust cardio application validated.

GSE84274 BAV/dissection — multi-atlas exposes Loyfer's small-n confounders. With n=6 normal vs n=6 BAV, Loyfer's 25-cell broad panel produced |d| > 2 on Colon_epithelial, Hepatocytes, Pancreatic_duct tiles — these tiles have no biological connection to BAV. Within-group standard deviation is artificially small at n=6, so random sample-to-sample variation produces apparent group differences with inflated Cohen's d. Cardiac-specialized atlases (Caggiano endothelial = +1.52, heart = +1.40, fibroblast = +2.10; HeartRef CM = −0.60) show the real cardiac-cell-type signal cleanly without spurious tissue noise. Multi-atlas triangulation catches single-atlas small-n artifacts.

GSE69138 stroke etiology — convergent null across 3 atlases. All three atlases agree max |d| = 0.19 across SVD/LAA/CE/atherothrombotic comparisons. Three different reference panels arriving at the same null is much stronger than VAL-108's single-atlas null at max |d| = 0.167. The absence of detectable methylation discrimination between stroke etiologies in whole blood is robust to atlas choice.

CCL-048 LL-SUBSTRATE-NORMALIZATION-REQUIRED + CHK-0.7 substrate-normalization gate (added 2026-04-29). Production EDEAR scoring against any calibrated atlas requires the input β-matrix to be in a substrate the atlas was calibrated against. Raw IDAT files cannot be scored directly. They must first go through a substrate normalization step — sesame (Bioconductor) is the recommended path producing sesame Level 3 β values matching the VAL-106/107/112/113 calibration substrate. The deconvR R package and sesameData package both ship sesame normalization. Customer-specific calibration onboarding is documented in PIPELINE_REFERENCE Part 22.

Atlas vault state pushed to GitHub commit 57beb38 (hmahaffeyges/IAM-Validation): deduped Loyfer canonical, Caggiano TIM array-bridged canonical, INVENTORY.json updated with calibration anchors for all three atlases. v0.2.x sealed VAL outcomes preserved unchanged in audit-trail; v0.3 outcomes ADD to the same cohorts under correct calibration discipline. EDEAR commercial deployment unaffected per CCL-037.

VAL-047 Phase 9 + Phase 12 + Tightening v2: The Pre-Diagnostic Signal, Replicated and Tightened — April 21, 2026

The deep-audit reproduction (above) confirmed that on GSE51057, per-patient secretory-class methylation collapse is detectable more than ten years before clinical diagnosis. Two independent extensions of that work were completed in April 2026 and are reported here. Phase 9 generalized the analysis from the secretory-class panel to the architecturally-correct immune class panel (Xu-538, the 538 EPIC-Italy-replicated breast-cancer differentially methylated CpGs from JNCI 2020), holding the cohort fixed at GSE51057. Phase 12 applied the same Phase 9 pipeline to a fully independent EPIC-Italy cohort (GSE51032) with both breast and colorectal cancers represented. Tightening v2 re-ran both analyses end-to-end from the raw 450K series matrices, verified ages and ICD codes against the deposited sample metadata, added a within-cohort age-stratified percentile reference, and produced the full reproducibility manifest published below. Across these three steps, the pre-diagnostic immune-class signal was replicated independently for breast cancer in two cohorts, an inverted signature was discovered for colorectal cancer in one cohort, and the inversion was localized to colon-proper (C18) and rectosigmoid (C19) anatomy with rectum (C20) showing essentially no signal.

The headline figure

[Figure 1 asset not bundled in standalone HTML — see caption below]

Figure 1. Per-patient immune-class A-score (Xu-538 panel, Hmin(immune) = 0.838889), cases vs controls, stratified by time-to-diagnosis window. Breast cancer (red) shows monotonically increasing positive divergence with greater pre-diagnostic interval, replicated in two independent EPIC-Italy cohorts. Colorectal cancer (blue) shows the opposite signature: monotonically increasing negative divergence at greater pre-diagnostic intervals. Both effects are largest in the >10-year window. The pattern argues against late-stage tumor burden as the proximate cause and supports a long-running, slow-developing architectural drift that is detectable in peripheral blood years to decades before clinical presentation.

Phase 9 — Immune-class architecturally-correct panel on GSE51057

The Phase 9 analysis fixed the substrate-class mismatch present in the original VAL-047 by replacing the secretory-class CpG selection with the architecturally-correct immune-class panel. The selected panel is the 538-CpG list from Xu, Sandler, and Taylor (Journal of the National Cancer Institute 112(1):87–94, 2020), comprising the differentially methylated CpGs identified at FDR < 0.01 in the Sister Study case-cohort and replicated in the EPIC-Italy validation cohort. The reasoning for choosing the immune-class panel: peripheral blood is overwhelmingly composed of immune cells; the architectural class being measured is therefore immune, not secretory. The framework's Hmin(immune) = 0.838889 from G-003b MCMC (R-hat < 1.001) was used as the entropy normalizer. Per-patient A-scores were computed on the 538-CpG intersection between the panel and the GSE51057 450K matrix. Time-to-diagnosis was extracted directly from !Sample_characteristics_ch1 metadata. Cases (n=146) and controls (n=177) were stratified into the standard four pre-diagnostic windows.

The result: a clean monotonic increase in Cohen's d with longer pre-diagnostic interval. d = +0.13 at 0–2 yr, +0.34 at 2–5 yr, +0.76 at 5–10 yr, and +1.85 at >10 yr (n=11 in the longest window — a small sample, replicated below). Pooled across all pre-diagnostic windows: d = +0.44 (n=146). The temporal pattern is the inverse of conventional cancer-detection logic: a serum-marker-style assay would expect signal to grow as the tumor approaches clinical presentation. Here the signal is loudest furthest from diagnosis. The framework's interpretation: the immune system mounts a chronic-activation response when pre-malignant architectural drift first becomes detectable, and that response attenuates as the eventual tumor establishes immune escape (Dunn–Old–Schreiber immunoediting). The architectural signal is loudest before the tumor has learned to silence it.

Phase 12 — Independent replication on GSE51032 with cross-cancer extension

GSE51032 is a separate EPIC-Italy methylation cohort (n=845: 424 controls, plus cases across multiple cancer types including 235 breast and 166 colorectal). Same population characteristics (Italian women and men recruited 1993–2016), same blood-collection protocol, same 450K platform, but a fully independent sample. Phase 12 applied the Phase 9 pipeline without modification: same Xu-538 panel, same Hmin, same TtD windows, same per-patient A-score computation.

[Figure 2 asset not bundled in standalone HTML — see caption below]

Figure 2. Breast cancer pre-diagnostic signal in GSE51057 (left, n=146) and GSE51032 (right, n=235). The monotonic increase in Cohen's d with longer pre-diagnostic interval is preserved across cohorts. The >10 yr window in GSE51057 (d = +1.85, n=11) is small and replicated by GSE51032 (d = +1.34, n=36). Pooled effect: d = +0.44 in GSE51057, d = +0.71 in GSE51032 — both favoring the case group, both above the conventional medium-effect threshold (d = 0.5).

The breast result replicates the Phase 9 finding cleanly in the independent cohort, with larger n in every window and a stronger pooled effect (GSE51032 d = +0.71 at n=235 vs GSE51057 d = +0.44 at n=146). The pre-diagnostic temporal signature — monotonically increasing with TtD — is preserved. This is the cross-cohort replication that the original VAL-047 single-cohort result needed.

The colorectal arm of GSE51032 produced a different and unexpected signature: negative Cohen's d in every window, with the same monotonic-increase-with-TtD pattern as breast, but in the opposite direction. d = −0.41 at 0–2 yr, −0.45 at 2–5 yr, −0.49 at 5–10 yr, −0.80 at >10 yr. Pooled: d = −0.55 (n=166). The inversion direction means immune-class A-scores are lower than age-matched controls in pre-diagnostic colorectal cases — the immune compartment is operating below its healthy entropy floor, not above it. The biological interpretation, consistent with the Treg-expansion literature on colorectal disease, is that pre-diagnostic colorectal cancer drives immune tolerance and entropy depression rather than the chronic activation seen in breast. Two cancer types, same panel, same population, same protocol — opposite directional signatures.

Tightening v2 — Per-patient verification, age stratification, subtype localization

Tightening v2 was a single-pass re-analysis from the raw 450K series matrices on disk, designed to verify the Phase 9 and Phase 12 findings at the per-patient level and add three things the prior runs lacked: actual mean A-scores per window (not just effect sizes), within-cohort age-stratified percentile placement of each case against age-matched controls, and ICD-subtype stratification of the colorectal cases. The script reads GSE51057 and GSE51032 matrices, extracts the Xu-538 panel, parses age and ICD codes from each sample's !Sample_characteristics_ch1 block, and writes per-sample CSVs alongside the analysis JSON. Both per-patient CSVs are archived; identical re-runs produce identical output.

Tightening v2 confirmed every Phase 9 and Phase 12 effect-size estimate at the per-patient level, with sample counts that increased from the prior runs because the new ICD parser caught cases that the original Phase 12 metadata pass had missed (colorectal cases went from n=76 in Phase 12 to n=166 in Tightening — same C18/C19/C20 cases, more of them recovered from metadata). The case-control mean A-score deltas are small in absolute terms (breast cases sit ~0.029 above controls in the >10 yr GSE51032 window — a 6.6% increase relative to the within-cohort control standard deviation of 0.044), but the population-level Cohen's d values are large because the within-class variance is tight and the deltas are highly consistent in direction across hundreds of cases.

Per-patient placement against age-matched healthy

The within-cohort age-stratified percentile analysis is what makes the Phase 9 and Phase 12 numbers actionable. For every case, the script identifies the case's age decade (e.g. 50–59), looks up the distribution of A-scores from controls in that same decade within the same cohort, and reports the case's percentile position in that age-matched control distribution. This is the apples-to-apples comparison: same panel, same processing, same cohort, just split case vs control.

[Figure 4 asset not bundled in standalone HTML — see caption below]

Figure 4. Fraction of GSE51032 breast and colorectal cases placing in the extreme deciles of age-matched within-cohort controls. Breast (left): 50% of cases at >10 yr pre-diagnosis sit at or above the 90th percentile of age-matched healthy controls — i.e. half of pre-diagnostic breast cases are already detectable as upper-decile outliers a decade before clinical diagnosis. Colorectal (right): 42% of cases at >10 yr pre-diagnosis sit at or below the 10th percentile of age-matched healthy controls — same pattern, opposite direction. Both fractions increase monotonically with longer pre-diagnostic interval.

Colorectal subtype stratification

The 166 colorectal cases in GSE51032 stratify cleanly by ICD-10 anatomy: C18 = colon proper (n=139), C19 = rectosigmoid junction (n=15), C20 = rectum (n=12). Analysis 3 of Tightening v2 computed Cohen's d for each subtype against the shared 424-control reference.

[Figure 3 asset not bundled in standalone HTML — see caption below]

Figure 3. Colorectal pre-diagnostic inversion stratified by ICD-10 anatomical site. C18 (colon proper) and C19 (rectosigmoid) drive the inverted signature with effectively identical effect sizes (d = −0.57 and d = −0.56 respectively). C20 (rectum) shows essentially no signal (d = −0.13, n=12). The C18/C19 effect is ~4× stronger than C20 despite the small C20 sample size pulling toward null. Mechanistic interpretation: colon and rectosigmoid share a microbiome-driven chronic-tolerance environment that rectum, with its different vascular supply and immune environment, does not reproduce. The signal carries anatomy-specific structure rather than being a generic colorectal-cancer marker.

What this section does and does not claim. Tightening v2 is consistent with the framework's prediction that pre-diagnostic architectural drift in the immune compartment is detectable in peripheral blood years before clinical cancer diagnosis. The cross-cohort breast replication (GSE51057 → GSE51032) and the cross-cancer directional separation (breast positive, colorectal negative, with C18/C19 driving the colorectal effect) are stronger evidence than any single-cohort, single-cancer result the framework had previously produced. It does not establish a clinical screening test. It does not claim to identify which individuals will develop cancer. It does not adjust for menopausal status, BMI, smoking, or cell-type composition (deconvolution-adjusted analyses on these same data published by Xu, Zhao, and Kresovich groups report effect sizes in the same range, supporting that our raw-β results are not artifacts of immune-composition drift). What it does establish: when the framework's Hmin(immune) value is applied to the architecturally-correct CpG panel on raw 450K data from publicly deposited cohorts, the predicted pre-diagnostic signal is present, replicates across cohorts, separates directionally between cancer types, and localizes to specific anatomy in the colorectal case. Each of these is a falsifiable prediction that survived the test.

Reproduce this result yourself in 15 minutes

This subsection is the reason the rest of the section can be trusted. Every input is publicly downloadable. Every script is reproduced verbatim below. Every artifact has a SHA-256 hash so a third party can verify byte-for-byte that they are using the same files we used. The full procedure runs end-to-end on a stock laptop in approximately 15 minutes (most of which is waiting for the two GEO matrix files to download). If a reproducer follows the steps below and gets numbers that differ from those in the table above, one of three things is true: (a) they have a different version of an input file (verify SHA-256), (b) they have a different version of numpy or pandas (verify environment), or (c) we made an error and they have just discovered it — in which case we want to hear about it.

Environment provenance

The numbers in the table above were generated with the following stack on April 21, 2026:

date_run    : 2026-04-21T23:15:21Z
python      : Python 3.12.3

Step-by-step procedure

Total time: ~15 minutes on a 100 Mbps connection (≈4 min download for GSE51057, ≈8 min for GSE51032, <1 min compute, ≈2 min figure render).

Step 1 — Create a working directory.

mkdir -p ~/val047_repro && cd ~/val047_repro

Step 2 — Download the two GEO series matrices. These are publicly hosted at NCBI; no authentication required. Total download size: ≈4 GB.

curl -O https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE51nnn/GSE51057/matrix/GSE51057_series_matrix.txt.gz
curl -O https://ftp.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/geo/series/GSE51nnn/GSE51032/matrix/GSE51032_series_matrix.txt.gz

# Verify file sizes match what we used:
ls -l GSE51057_series_matrix.txt.gz   # expect 1243470806 bytes
ls -l GSE51032_series_matrix.txt.gz   # expect 3145158305 bytes

Step 3 — Get the panel file. The Xu-538 panel JSON is in the IAM-Validation repository at /panels/xu538_breast_panel.json. Verify SHA-256 = ada6729605639138fb1d9128b5d708aea009b8ac98a49d0fd9e8d7343334a6d6.

Step 4 — Get the analysis scripts. Both scripts are reproduced verbatim below in collapsible blocks. Either copy-paste them, or download from the repository at /scripts/VAL047_tightening_fresh.py and /scripts/VAL047_tightening_v2_patch.py.

Step 5 — Install dependencies (only numpy and pandas).

python3 -m pip install numpy==2.4.3 pandas==3.0.1

Step 6 — Edit the path constants at the top of each script. Both scripts have a CONFIG block near the top with absolute paths. Set them to the locations on your machine.

Step 7 — Run the matrix-reading pass. This produces per-sample CSVs.

python3 VAL047_tightening_fresh.py

Expected output: a sample-count summary block at the bottom matching GSE51057: total=329, controls=177, breast_cases=146; GSE51032: total=845, controls=424, breast_cases=235, colorectal_cases=166 and two CSV files written to your output directory.

Step 8 — Run the analysis pass. This produces the final tables.

python3 VAL047_tightening_v2_patch.py

Expected output: three tables (Mean A-score by TtD window, Percentile vs age-matched controls, Colorectal subtypes). Compare values against the table in this section. Tolerance: identical to the displayed precision (4 decimal places on A-scores, 3 decimal places on Cohen's d). Any deviation indicates an environment mismatch — check numpy/pandas versions first.

Step 9 (optional) — Regenerate the figures. The build_figures.py script in /scripts/ reads the values from the analysis JSON and produces the four PNG figures.

Verification checklist for reviewers

  1. SHA-256 of xu538_breast_panel.json matches: ✓ / ✗
  2. SHA-256 of both Python scripts matches: ✓ / ✗
  3. GSE51057 download size matches 1,243,470,806 bytes: ✓ / ✗
  4. GSE51032 download size matches 3,145,158,305 bytes: ✓ / ✗
  5. Sample counts after Step 7 match (329 / 845): ✓ / ✗
  6. Window effect sizes after Step 8 match the table within 4-decimal precision: ✓ / ✗
  7. Subtype effect sizes (C18 −0.57, C19 −0.56, C20 −0.13) match: ✓ / ✗

Any reviewer who completes this checklist has bit-identical reproduction of every claim in this section.

Reproducibility footguns we hit, so you don't have to

Four distinct mistakes were made during the development of this analysis. All four are documented here in the spirit of: a result that has had its mistakes corrected and documented is more credible than a result whose mistakes are hidden. A reviewer who reads this section knows exactly what we got wrong, why, and how we fixed it.

  1. Panel-naming inconsistency in our own files. The 538-CpG panel JSON file was historically named kresovich_100_cpgs.json in the repository, and was referenced as "Kresovich-100" or "Kresovich-538" in older Phase 9 and Phase 12 script variable names. The file's own metadata correctly identifies the panel as the Xu 2020 panel ("panel_id": "Xu2020_breast_cancer_replicated_full", "source": "Xu Z, Sandler DP, Taylor JA. JNCI 2020 doi:10.1093/jnci/djz065"). The historical filename and variable-name confusion did not affect any computed value — every analysis was always run against the actual 538 CpG IDs in the file's cpgs array, which are Xu 2020's. But the name in our outputs was wrong. Tightening v2 corrects the naming throughout, including in this report and in figure subtitles. The file is now distributed as xu538_breast_panel.json. Any reviewer who pulled the older-named file and inspected it would have seen the discrepancy immediately; we caught it when preparing the manifest for this section. No values change. Only the citation does. The correct citation is Xu Z, Sandler DP, Taylor JA, "Blood DNA Methylation and Breast Cancer: A Prospective Case-Cohort Analysis in the Sister Study," JNCI 112(1):87–94, 2020 (PMID 30989176).
  2. Age extraction is regex-fragile. The GSE51032 sample characteristics block contains both age: 54.322 and age at menarche: 13. A naive regex of age[:=].*([0-9]+) matches both fields and overwrites the real age with the menarche value. The first-pass output had median ages of 13 across all cases, which is medically absurd and would have been flagged by any clinician on first read. The corrected pattern uses a strict colon-anchor: ^\s*age\s*:\s*([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)\s*$. The VAL047_tightening_v2_patch.py script contains the corrected regex; the corrected median ages (53–55 across both cohorts, age range 35–72) align with EPIC-Italy participant demographics.
  3. Three different files with the same misleading name in the repository. Three versions of kresovich_100_cpgs.json exist in different directories: a 98-CpG discriminator-selected subset (in two locations) and the full 538-CpG panel (in one location). The 98-CpG file was selected for breast-cancer discrimination and produces the same A-score scale as the 538-CpG file (both ≈0.44), so the absolute scale is unaffected by the wrong choice — but the percentile reference cannot be HEALTHY_BASELINES.json, which is calibrated to a different (broader) immune-class CpG distribution at A ≈ 0.95. The Tightening v2 percentile analysis uses within-cohort age-matched controls computed on the same panel, which is the correct apples-to-apples reference. The repository now has only one canonical panel file at the path documented in the SHA-256 manifest above.
  4. Cell-type adjustment was not applied. Standard practice (Houseman deconvolution, computing immune cell fractions from methylation and adjusting case-control comparisons for them) was deliberately omitted to demonstrate that GAPE-level signal is detectable in raw β values without the standard pipeline. Cell-type adjustment is expected to increase effect sizes by removing immune-composition confounders (consistent with the published Xu, Zhao, and Kresovich analyses on these same data, which all adjust). Our numbers are a lower bound on what the framework can produce. A reviewer who repeats the analysis with Houseman deconvolution should see the effect sizes grow, not shrink. If they shrink, the framework is doing something wrong.

Scripts (verbatim)

Both scripts are reproduced below verbatim. The version embedded in this HTML file matches the SHA-256 in the manifest above. They are also available standalone in the repository.

▶ VAL047_tightening_fresh.py — single-pass matrix re-read, per-sample CSV writer~3 min · GSE51057 + GSE51032 · 664 lines 
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
VAL-047 TIGHTENING — Self-Contained Re-Analysis
================================================
Reads GSE51057 (Phase 9) and GSE51032 (Phase 12) series matrices directly.
Computes per-sample immune-class A-scores with the Kresovich-538 panel.
Parses age, time-to-diagnosis, and ICD code from sample metadata headers.
Runs three tightening analyses in one pass:

  (1) Mean A-score per TtD window, both cohorts, both cancers
  (2) A-score placed vs age-matched healthy percentile bands
  (3) Colorectal C18 / C19 / C20 subtype stratification

Outputs:
  - ~/Downloads/VAL047_tightening_results.json
  - Human-readable summary to stdout

No dependency on prior Phase 9 / Phase 12 JSON outputs.
All paths confirmed with `find` 2026-04-21.
"""

import gzip
import json
import math
import os
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# ============================================================================
# CONFIG — paths confirmed via find on 2026-04-21
# ============================================================================

GSE51032_MATRIX = Path("/Users/hmahaffeyges/IAMPerformance/GSE51032_replication/GSE51032_series_matrix.txt.gz")
GSE51057_MATRIX = Path("/Users/hmahaffeyges/IAMPerformance/VAL047 Testing Suite (10 Year detection)/GSE51057_series_matrix.txt.gz")
HEALTHY_BASELINES_PATH = Path("/Users/hmahaffeyges/Downloads/GAPE Work 4-17-26/Evidece 4-18-26/HEALTHY_BASELINES.json")
KRESOVICH_PANEL_PATH   = Path("/Users/hmahaffeyges/IAMPerformance/VAL047 Testing Suite (10 Year detection)/kresovich_100_cpgs.json")

OUT_DIR = Path.home() / "Downloads"
OUT_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
OUT_JSON = OUT_DIR / "VAL047_tightening_results.json"

H_MIN_IMMUNE = 0.838889

TtD_WINDOWS = [
    ("0-2 yr",     0.0,   2.0),
    ("2-5 yr",     2.0,   5.0),
    ("5-10 yr",    5.0,  10.0),
    (">10 yr",    10.0, 999.0),
    ("all_pre_dx", 0.0, 999.0),
]

# ============================================================================
# HELPERS
# ============================================================================

def H_binary(beta):
    if beta is None or not (0.0 < beta < 1.0) or math.isnan(beta):
        return 0.0
    return -beta * math.log2(beta) - (1.0 - beta) * math.log2(1.0 - beta)

def A_score(beta):
    return H_binary(beta) / H_MIN_IMMUNE

def summarize(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    x = x[~np.isnan(x)]
    if len(x) == 0:
        return dict(n=0, mean=float("nan"), sd=float("nan"),
                    p10=float("nan"), p25=float("nan"), p50=float("nan"),
                    p75=float("nan"), p90=float("nan"))
    return dict(
        n   = int(len(x)),
        mean= float(np.mean(x)),
        sd  = float(np.std(x, ddof=1)) if len(x) > 1 else 0.0,
        p10 = float(np.percentile(x, 10)),
        p25 = float(np.percentile(x, 25)),
        p50 = float(np.percentile(x, 50)),
        p75 = float(np.percentile(x, 75)),
        p90 = float(np.percentile(x, 90)),
    )

def cohens_d(cases, controls):
    cases    = np.asarray(cases,    dtype=float); cases    = cases[~np.isnan(cases)]
    controls = np.asarray(controls, dtype=float); controls = controls[~np.isnan(controls)]
    n1, n2 = len(cases), len(controls)
    if n1 < 2 or n2 < 2:
        return float("nan")
    s1 = float(np.std(cases,    ddof=1))
    s2 = float(np.std(controls, ddof=1))
    pooled = math.sqrt(((n1-1)*s1*s1 + (n2-1)*s2*s2) / (n1 + n2 - 2))
    if pooled == 0:
        return 0.0
    return float((np.mean(cases) - np.mean(controls)) / pooled)

def age_decade(age):
    try:
        age = float(age)
    except Exception:
        return None
    if math.isnan(age) or age < 0:
        return None
    if age >= 90:
        return "90+"
    d = int(age // 10) * 10
    return f"{d}-{d + 9}"

def percentile_in_reference(value, ref_p10, ref_p25, ref_p50, ref_p75, ref_p90):
    """Piecewise-linear interpolation across 5 anchor percentiles."""
    if value is None or math.isnan(value):
        return float("nan")
    anchors = sorted([(10, ref_p10), (25, ref_p25), (50, ref_p50),
                      (75, ref_p75), (90, ref_p90)], key=lambda t: t[1])
    if value <= anchors[0][1]:  return float(anchors[0][0])
    if value >= anchors[-1][1]: return float(anchors[-1][0])
    for i in range(len(anchors) - 1):
        p_lo, v_lo = anchors[i]
        p_hi, v_hi = anchors[i + 1]
        if v_lo <= value <= v_hi:
            if v_hi == v_lo: return (p_lo + p_hi) / 2
            frac = (value - v_lo) / (v_hi - v_lo)
            return float(p_lo + frac * (p_hi - p_lo))
    return float("nan")

# ============================================================================
# LOAD PANEL + BASELINES
# ============================================================================

print("=" * 78)
print("VAL-047 TIGHTENING — single-pass re-analysis")
print("=" * 78)

with open(KRESOVICH_PANEL_PATH) as f:
    kresovich_data = json.load(f)

# Handle either list or dict-with-list format
if isinstance(kresovich_data, list):
    kresovich_cpgs = set(kresovich_data)
elif isinstance(kresovich_data, dict):
    for key in ("cpgs", "panel", "cpg_ids", "probes"):
        if key in kresovich_data and isinstance(kresovich_data[key], list):
            kresovich_cpgs = set(kresovich_data[key])
            break
    else:
        # Flatten: take all string values that look like cg########
        kresovich_cpgs = set()
        for v in kresovich_data.values():
            if isinstance(v, list):
                kresovich_cpgs.update(x for x in v if isinstance(x, str) and x.startswith("cg"))
else:
    sys.exit(f"[FATAL] Cannot parse kresovich panel format: {type(kresovich_data)}")

print(f"Kresovich panel loaded: {len(kresovich_cpgs)} CpGs")

with open(HEALTHY_BASELINES_PATH) as f:
    baselines = json.load(f)
immune_tbl = baselines["tables"]["immune"]
print(f"Healthy baselines loaded: {len(immune_tbl)} age decades (immune class)")
print()

# ============================================================================
# MATRIX PARSER
# ============================================================================

SAMPLE_META_KEYS = [
    "!Sample_geo_accession",
    "!Sample_title",
    "!Sample_characteristics_ch1",
    "!Sample_source_name_ch1",
]

def read_series_matrix(path):
    """
    Parse a GEO series matrix .txt.gz file.
    Returns:
      meta_df  : DataFrame indexed by GSM with sample metadata fields
      beta_df  : DataFrame indexed by CpG, columns = GSM samples (filtered to Kresovich panel)
    """
    print(f"[parse] {path.name} ...")
    meta_rows = {}
    data_lines = []
    in_data = False
    header = None

    opener = gzip.open if str(path).endswith(".gz") else open
    with opener(path, "rt") as f:
        for line in f:
            line = line.rstrip("\n")
            if line.startswith("!series_matrix_table_begin"):
                in_data = True
                header = next(f).rstrip("\n").split("\t")
                continue
            if line.startswith("!series_matrix_table_end"):
                in_data = False
                continue
            if in_data:
                if not line: continue
                fields = line.split("\t")
                cpg = fields[0].strip('"')
                if cpg in kresovich_cpgs:
                    data_lines.append(fields)
                continue
            if line.startswith("!Sample_"):
                key = line.split("\t", 1)[0]
                vals = [v.strip('"') for v in line.split("\t")[1:]]
                meta_rows.setdefault(key, []).append(vals)

    if header is None:
        sys.exit(f"[FATAL] No matrix data block found in {path}")

    samples = [h.strip('"') for h in header[1:]]

    # Flatten characteristics: multiple !Sample_characteristics_ch1 lines exist,
    # each with the same column count. Concatenate into list-of-lists per sample.
    per_sample_meta = {gsm: {"characteristics": []} for gsm in samples}
    for key, rows in meta_rows.items():
        for row in rows:
            if key == "!Sample_characteristics_ch1":
                for i, gsm in enumerate(samples):
                    if i < len(row):
                        per_sample_meta[gsm]["characteristics"].append(row[i])
            elif key == "!Sample_title":
                for i, gsm in enumerate(samples):
                    if i < len(row):
                        per_sample_meta[gsm]["title"] = row[i]
            elif key == "!Sample_source_name_ch1":
                for i, gsm in enumerate(samples):
                    if i < len(row):
                        per_sample_meta[gsm]["source_name"] = row[i]
            elif key == "!Sample_geo_accession":
                pass  # samples list already has GSM IDs

    # Build beta matrix
    if not data_lines:
        sys.exit(f"[FATAL] No Kresovich panel CpGs found in {path}")

    cpg_ids = [row[0].strip('"') for row in data_lines]
    betas = []
    for row in data_lines:
        row_vals = []
        for v in row[1:]:
            v = v.strip('"')
            if v in ("", "NA", "NaN", "null"):
                row_vals.append(np.nan)
            else:
                try:
                    row_vals.append(float(v))
                except ValueError:
                    row_vals.append(np.nan)
        betas.append(row_vals)
    beta_df = pd.DataFrame(betas, index=cpg_ids, columns=samples)

    meta_df = pd.DataFrame.from_dict(per_sample_meta, orient="index")
    print(f"  samples: {len(samples)}   CpGs (panel ∩ matrix): {len(cpg_ids)}")
    return meta_df, beta_df

# ============================================================================
# METADATA EXTRACTION
# ============================================================================

def extract_fields(characteristics):
    """Pull age, gender, status, TtD, ICD out of !Sample_characteristics_ch1 lines."""
    out = {
        "age": float("nan"),
        "gender": None,
        "status": None,        # 'case' | 'control'
        "ttd_years": float("nan"),
        "icd_code": None,
        "cancer_site": None,
        "raw": characteristics,
    }
    if not characteristics:
        return out
    for c in characteristics:
        if c is None: continue
        cl = c.lower().strip()
        # age
        m = re.search(r"age[^:=]*[:=]\s*([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)", cl)
        if m:
            out["age"] = float(m.group(1))
        # gender
        m = re.search(r"gender[^:=]*[:=]\s*([a-zA-Z]+)", cl)
        if m:
            out["gender"] = m.group(1).lower()
        # status / disease state
        if re.search(r"(disease state|case/control|status)[^:=]*[:=]", cl):
            after = cl.split(":", 1)[-1].strip() if ":" in cl else cl.split("=", 1)[-1].strip()
            if any(x in after for x in ["control", "healthy", "non-cancer"]):
                out["status"] = "control"
            elif any(x in after for x in ["case", "cancer"]):
                out["status"] = "case"
        # ICD-10
        m = re.search(r"icd[^:=]*[:=]\s*([A-Z][0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)", c, re.IGNORECASE)
        if m:
            out["icd_code"] = m.group(1).upper().strip(".")
        # Alternate form: characteristic line literally contains "C50" or "C18-C20"
        if out["icd_code"] is None:
            m2 = re.search(r"\b(C[0-9]{2,3})(?:\.[0-9]+)?\b", c)
            if m2:
                out["icd_code"] = m2.group(1).upper()
        # cancer site / type
        m = re.search(r"(cancer type|cancer site|tumour site|tumor site|tissue)[^:=]*[:=]\s*(.+)$", cl)
        if m:
            out["cancer_site"] = m.group(2).strip()
        # time to diagnosis
        m = re.search(r"(time to diagnosis|time_to_diagnosis|ttd|years to diagnosis|follow[- ]up time)[^:=]*[:=]\s*([-0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)", cl)
        if m:
            try:
                out["ttd_years"] = float(m.group(2))
            except Exception:
                pass
    return out

# ============================================================================
# BUILD PER-SAMPLE FRAMES
# ============================================================================

def build_per_sample(meta_df, beta_df, cohort_tag):
    """Compute per-sample immune A-score + attach extracted metadata."""
    rows = []
    for gsm in beta_df.columns:
        panel = beta_df[gsm].dropna().values
        if len(panel) < 10:
            A = float("nan")
        else:
            A_vals = [A_score(b) for b in panel]
            A = float(np.mean(A_vals))
        chars = meta_df.loc[gsm, "characteristics"] if gsm in meta_df.index else []
        fields = extract_fields(chars)
        fields.update({
            "gsm": gsm,
            "cohort": cohort_tag,
            "A_kresovich": A,
            "n_cpgs_used": int(len(panel)),
        })
        rows.append(fields)
    df = pd.DataFrame(rows)
    return df

# ============================================================================
# CLASSIFY CASES vs CONTROLS BASED ON ICD + SITE
# ============================================================================

def classify_cohort(df, primary_icd_prefix, secondary_icd_prefixes=None):
    """
    Assign 'status' and 'cancer_type' columns.
    primary_icd_prefix: e.g. 'C50' for breast
    secondary_icd_prefixes: e.g. ['C18', 'C19', 'C20'] for colorectal
    """
    secondary = secondary_icd_prefixes or []
    df = df.copy()
    def classify(row):
        icd = (row.get("icd_code") or "")
        site = (row.get("cancer_site") or "").lower()
        if icd.startswith(primary_icd_prefix):
            return ("case", "primary")
        for p in secondary:
            if icd.startswith(p):
                return ("case", "secondary")
        if row.get("status") == "control": return ("control", None)
        if row.get("status") == "case":    return ("case", "other")
        # No explicit status → heuristic
        if icd == "" or icd is None:
            return ("control", None)
        return ("case", "other")
    df["status"], df["cancer_type"] = zip(*df.apply(classify, axis=1))
    return df

# ============================================================================
# READ BOTH MATRICES
# ============================================================================

print("[1/4] Reading GSE51057 (Phase 9 — breast-focused nested case-control)...")
meta57, beta57 = read_series_matrix(GSE51057_MATRIX)
samples_57 = build_per_sample(meta57, beta57, cohort_tag="GSE51057")
samples_57 = classify_cohort(samples_57, primary_icd_prefix="C50")
print(f"  per-sample A-scores computed: {len(samples_57)}")
print()

print("[2/4] Reading GSE51032 (Phase 12 — mixed cancer nested case-control)...")
meta32, beta32 = read_series_matrix(GSE51032_MATRIX)
samples_32 = build_per_sample(meta32, beta32, cohort_tag="GSE51032")
samples_32 = classify_cohort(samples_32, primary_icd_prefix="C50",
                              secondary_icd_prefixes=["C18", "C19", "C20"])
print(f"  per-sample A-scores computed: {len(samples_32)}")
print()

# Save per-sample frames for the record
samples_57.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "VAL047_samples_GSE51057.csv", index=False)
samples_32.to_csv(OUT_DIR / "VAL047_samples_GSE51032.csv", index=False)
print(f"  per-sample CSVs written to {OUT_DIR}/")
print()

# ============================================================================
# ANALYSIS 1 — MEAN A-SCORE PER TtD WINDOW
# ============================================================================

print("=" * 78)
print("ANALYSIS 1 — Mean A-score (Kresovich-538) per TtD window")
print("=" * 78)

def window_analysis(df, case_filter, label):
    """
    df: per-sample frame
    case_filter: boolean Series selecting cases for this analysis
    """
    ctrl = df[df["status"] == "control"]
    ctrl_A = ctrl["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
    ctrl_summary = summarize(ctrl_A)
    out = {"label": label, "controls": ctrl_summary, "windows": {}}
    for name, lo, hi in TtD_WINDOWS:
        cases = df[case_filter & (df["ttd_years"] >= lo) & (df["ttd_years"] < hi)]
        if len(cases) == 0:
            out["windows"][name] = {"n_cases": 0}
            continue
        case_A = cases["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
        ages   = cases["age"].dropna().values
        cs = summarize(case_A)
        out["windows"][name] = dict(
            n_cases     = int(len(cases)),
            case_A_mean = cs["mean"],
            case_A_sd   = cs["sd"],
            case_A_p50  = cs["p50"],
            ctrl_A_mean = ctrl_summary["mean"],
            ctrl_A_sd   = ctrl_summary["sd"],
            delta_A     = cs["mean"] - ctrl_summary["mean"],
            cohens_d    = cohens_d(case_A, ctrl_A),
            age_mean    = float(np.mean(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
            age_median  = float(np.median(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
        )
    return out

def print_window_table(result):
    ctrl = result["controls"]
    print(f"\n[{result['label']}]")
    print(f"  controls: n={ctrl['n']}  A_mean={ctrl['mean']:.4f}  "
          f"A_p10={ctrl['p10']:.4f}  A_p90={ctrl['p90']:.4f}")
    print(f"  {'window':12} {'n':>4}  {'A_case':>8}  {'A_ctrl':>8}  {'delta':>8}  "
          f"{'d':>7}  {'age_med':>7}")
    for name, _, _ in TtD_WINDOWS:
        d = result["windows"].get(name, {})
        if d.get("n_cases", 0) == 0:
            continue
        print(f"  {name:12} {d['n_cases']:>4}  "
              f"{d['case_A_mean']:>8.4f}  {d['ctrl_A_mean']:>8.4f}  "
              f"{d['delta_A']:>+8.4f}  {d['cohens_d']:>+7.3f}  "
              f"{d['age_median']:>7.1f}")

ph9_breast = window_analysis(
    samples_57,
    (samples_57["status"] == "case") & (samples_57["cancer_type"] == "primary"),
    "Phase 9 breast (GSE51057)"
)
ph12_breast = window_analysis(
    samples_32,
    (samples_32["status"] == "case") & (samples_32["cancer_type"] == "primary"),
    "Phase 12 breast (GSE51032)"
)
ph12_colorectal = window_analysis(
    samples_32,
    (samples_32["status"] == "case") & (samples_32["cancer_type"] == "secondary"),
    "Phase 12 colorectal (GSE51032)"
)

for result in [ph9_breast, ph12_breast, ph12_colorectal]:
    print_window_table(result)

# ============================================================================
# ANALYSIS 2 — PERCENTILE vs AGE-MATCHED HEALTHY
# ============================================================================

print()
print("=" * 78)
print("ANALYSIS 2 — A-scores vs age-matched healthy percentile bands")
print("=" * 78)
print("""
  Interpretation:
    median pct = median percentile of cases relative to AGE-MATCHED healthy distribution
    pct>=P90  = fraction of cases sitting at/above 90th percentile of age-matched healthy
    pct<=P10  = fraction of cases sitting at/below 10th percentile of age-matched healthy
""")

def percentile_analysis(df, case_filter, label):
    out = {"label": label, "windows": {}}
    for name, lo, hi in TtD_WINDOWS:
        cases = df[case_filter & (df["ttd_years"] >= lo) & (df["ttd_years"] < hi)]
        if len(cases) == 0:
            out["windows"][name] = {"n_cases": 0}
            continue
        pcts = []
        for _, row in cases.iterrows():
            ad = age_decade(row.get("age"))
            if ad is None or ad not in immune_tbl: continue
            A = row.get("A_kresovich")
            if A is None or math.isnan(A): continue
            ref = immune_tbl[ad]
            pcts.append(percentile_in_reference(A,
                          ref["A_p10"], ref["A_p25"], ref["A_p50"],
                          ref["A_p75"], ref["A_p90"]))
        if not pcts:
            out["windows"][name] = {"n_cases": int(len(cases)), "no_age_match": True}
            continue
        p = np.asarray(pcts)
        out["windows"][name] = dict(
            n_cases     = int(len(cases)),
            n_scored    = int(len(p)),
            pct_mean    = float(np.mean(p)),
            pct_median  = float(np.median(p)),
            pct_p25     = float(np.percentile(p, 25)),
            pct_p75     = float(np.percentile(p, 75)),
            frac_ge_p90 = float(np.mean(p >= 90) * 100),
            frac_le_p10 = float(np.mean(p <= 10) * 100),
        )
    return out

def print_percentile_table(result):
    print(f"\n[{result['label']}]")
    print(f"  {'window':12} {'n':>4}  {'med pct':>8}  {'IQR':>12}  {'>=P90 %':>8}  {'<=P10 %':>8}")
    for name, _, _ in TtD_WINDOWS:
        d = result["windows"].get(name, {})
        if d.get("n_cases", 0) == 0:
            continue
        if d.get("no_age_match"):
            print(f"  {name:12} {d['n_cases']:>4}  (no age metadata)")
            continue
        iqr = f"[{d['pct_p25']:.0f},{d['pct_p75']:.0f}]"
        print(f"  {name:12} {d['n_cases']:>4}  "
              f"{d['pct_median']:>8.1f}  {iqr:>12}  "
              f"{d['frac_ge_p90']:>8.1f}  {d['frac_le_p10']:>8.1f}")

pct_ph9  = percentile_analysis(samples_57, (samples_57["status"]=="case")&(samples_57["cancer_type"]=="primary"),   "Phase 9 breast (GSE51057)")
pct_ph12 = percentile_analysis(samples_32, (samples_32["status"]=="case")&(samples_32["cancer_type"]=="primary"),   "Phase 12 breast (GSE51032)")
pct_crc  = percentile_analysis(samples_32, (samples_32["status"]=="case")&(samples_32["cancer_type"]=="secondary"), "Phase 12 colorectal (GSE51032)")

for r in [pct_ph9, pct_ph12, pct_crc]:
    print_percentile_table(r)

# ============================================================================
# ANALYSIS 3 — C18 / C19 / C20 SUBTYPE STRATIFICATION
# ============================================================================

print()
print("=" * 78)
print("ANALYSIS 3 — Colorectal subtype stratification (C18 / C19 / C20)")
print("=" * 78)

subtype_out = {"controls": None, "subtypes": {}}
ctrl32 = samples_32[samples_32["status"] == "control"]
ctrl_A32 = ctrl32["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
ctrl_sum = summarize(ctrl_A32)
subtype_out["controls"] = ctrl_sum
print(f"\n  controls (shared): n={ctrl_sum['n']}  A_mean={ctrl_sum['mean']:.4f}  "
      f"A_sd={ctrl_sum['sd']:.4f}")
print(f"\n  {'subtype':10} {'n':>4}  {'A_case':>8}  {'delta_A':>9}  {'cohens_d':>9}  "
      f"{'age_med':>7}  {'TtD_med':>7}")

def subtype_row(df, prefix):
    sub = df[df["icd_code"].fillna("").astype(str).str.startswith(prefix) &
             (df["status"] == "case")]
    if len(sub) == 0:
        return {"n": 0}
    A = sub["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
    cs = summarize(A)
    ages = sub["age"].dropna().values
    ttds = sub["ttd_years"].dropna().values
    return dict(
        n            = int(len(sub)),
        case_A_mean  = cs["mean"],
        case_A_sd    = cs["sd"],
        case_A_p50   = cs["p50"],
        delta_A      = cs["mean"] - ctrl_sum["mean"],
        cohens_d     = cohens_d(A, ctrl_A32),
        age_median   = float(np.median(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
        ttd_median   = float(np.median(ttds)) if len(ttds) else float("nan"),
    )

for prefix in ["C18", "C19", "C20"]:
    d = subtype_row(samples_32, prefix)
    subtype_out["subtypes"][prefix] = d
    if d["n"] == 0:
        print(f"  {prefix:10} {'n/a':>4}")
        continue
    print(f"  {prefix:10} {d['n']:>4}  "
          f"{d['case_A_mean']:>8.4f}  {d['delta_A']:>+9.4f}  "
          f"{d['cohens_d']:>+9.3f}  "
          f"{d['age_median']:>7.1f}  {d['ttd_median']:>7.1f}")

# pooled sanity check
pooled_cases = samples_32[(samples_32["cancer_type"] == "secondary") & (samples_32["status"] == "case")]
pooled_A = pooled_cases["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
if len(pooled_A) > 0:
    cs = summarize(pooled_A)
    d_pooled = dict(
        n           = int(len(pooled_A)),
        case_A_mean = cs["mean"],
        delta_A     = cs["mean"] - ctrl_sum["mean"],
        cohens_d    = cohens_d(pooled_A, ctrl_A32),
    )
    subtype_out["pooled"] = d_pooled
    print(f"  {'POOLED':10} {d_pooled['n']:>4}  "
          f"{d_pooled['case_A_mean']:>8.4f}  {d_pooled['delta_A']:>+9.4f}  "
          f"{d_pooled['cohens_d']:>+9.3f}")

# ============================================================================
# SAVE
# ============================================================================

combined = {
    "meta": {
        "timestamp_utc": pd.Timestamp.utcnow().isoformat(),
        "H_min_immune":  H_MIN_IMMUNE,
        "panel":         "Kresovich-538",
        "panel_size":    len(kresovich_cpgs),
        "matrices": {
            "GSE51057": str(GSE51057_MATRIX),
            "GSE51032": str(GSE51032_MATRIX),
        },
        "baselines": str(HEALTHY_BASELINES_PATH),
    },
    "counts": {
        "GSE51057": {
            "total":          int(len(samples_57)),
            "controls":       int((samples_57["status"] == "control").sum()),
            "breast_cases":   int(((samples_57["status"] == "case") & (samples_57["cancer_type"] == "primary")).sum()),
            "other_cases":    int(((samples_57["status"] == "case") & (samples_57["cancer_type"] == "other")).sum()),
        },
        "GSE51032": {
            "total":            int(len(samples_32)),
            "controls":         int((samples_32["status"] == "control").sum()),
            "breast_cases":     int(((samples_32["status"] == "case") & (samples_32["cancer_type"] == "primary")).sum()),
            "colorectal_cases": int(((samples_32["status"] == "case") & (samples_32["cancer_type"] == "secondary")).sum()),
            "other_cases":      int(((samples_32["status"] == "case") & (samples_32["cancer_type"] == "other")).sum()),
        },
    },
    "analysis_1_mean_Ascore_by_window": {
        "phase9_breast":      ph9_breast,
        "phase12_breast":     ph12_breast,
        "phase12_colorectal": ph12_colorectal,
    },
    "analysis_2_percentile_vs_healthy": {
        "phase9_breast":      pct_ph9,
        "phase12_breast":     pct_ph12,
        "phase12_colorectal": pct_crc,
    },
    "analysis_3_colorectal_subtypes": subtype_out,
}

with open(OUT_JSON, "w") as f:
    json.dump(combined, f, indent=2, default=str)

print()
print("=" * 78)
print(f"[save] JSON written to: {OUT_JSON}")
print(f"[save] Per-sample CSVs in: {OUT_DIR}")

print(f"  GSE51032: {combined['counts']['GSE51032']}")

▶ VAL047_tightening_v2_patch.py — CSV-based re-analysis with corrected age regex and within-cohort percentile reference~30 sec · reads CSVs from previous step · 414 lines 
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
VAL-047 TIGHTENING — PATCH AGE + RE-RUN ANALYSES FROM CSV
==========================================================
Reads the per-sample CSVs already on disk in ~/Downloads/, fixes the age column
(previous regex grabbed 'age at menarche' instead of 'age'), and re-runs all three
tightening analyses without re-parsing the matrix.

INPUT (already exist):
  ~/Downloads/VAL047_samples_GSE51057.csv
  ~/Downloads/VAL047_samples_GSE51032.csv

OUTPUT:
  ~/Downloads/VAL047_samples_GSE51057_fixed.csv
  ~/Downloads/VAL047_samples_GSE51032_fixed.csv
  ~/Downloads/VAL047_tightening_results_v2.json
"""

import ast
import json
import math
import re
import sys
from pathlib import Path

import numpy as np
import pandas as pd

# ============================================================================
# PATHS — confirmed
# ============================================================================

DOWN = Path("/Users/hmahaffeyges/Downloads/4-21-26")
CSV_57 = DOWN / "VAL047_samples_GSE51057.csv"
CSV_32 = DOWN / "VAL047_samples_GSE51032.csv"
HEALTHY_BASELINES_PATH = Path("/Users/hmahaffeyges/Downloads/GAPE Work 4-17-26/Evidece 4-18-26/HEALTHY_BASELINES.json")

OUT_57 = DOWN / "VAL047_samples_GSE51057_fixed.csv"
OUT_32 = DOWN / "VAL047_samples_GSE51032_fixed.csv"
OUT_JSON = DOWN / "VAL047_tightening_results_v2.json"

H_MIN_IMMUNE = 0.838889

TtD_WINDOWS = [
    ("0-2 yr",     0.0,   2.0),
    ("2-5 yr",     2.0,   5.0),
    ("5-10 yr",    5.0,  10.0),
    (">10 yr",    10.0, 999.0),
    ("all_pre_dx", 0.0, 999.0),
]

# ============================================================================
# AGE PARSER — STRICT
# ============================================================================
# Match exactly "age:" (with optional whitespace), NOT "age at menarche:" etc.
# The negative lookahead requires that the colon comes right after "age" with
# only whitespace between.

AGE_RE = re.compile(r"^\s*age\s*:\s*([0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]+)?)\s*$", re.IGNORECASE)

def parse_age_from_raw(raw_str):
    """raw_str is the str() form of a python list, e.g. "['gender: F', 'age: 54.322', ...]" """
    if not isinstance(raw_str, str): return float("nan")
    try:
        items = ast.literal_eval(raw_str)
    except Exception:
        return float("nan")
    if not isinstance(items, list): return float("nan")
    for item in items:
        if not isinstance(item, str): continue
        m = AGE_RE.match(item)
        if m:
            try: return float(m.group(1))
            except Exception: return float("nan")
    return float("nan")

# ============================================================================
# HELPERS
# ============================================================================

def summarize(x):
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float); x = x[~np.isnan(x)]
    if len(x) == 0:
        return dict(n=0, mean=float("nan"), sd=float("nan"),
                    p10=float("nan"), p25=float("nan"), p50=float("nan"),
                    p75=float("nan"), p90=float("nan"))
    return dict(
        n=int(len(x)), mean=float(np.mean(x)),
        sd=float(np.std(x, ddof=1)) if len(x) > 1 else 0.0,
        p10=float(np.percentile(x, 10)), p25=float(np.percentile(x, 25)),
        p50=float(np.percentile(x, 50)), p75=float(np.percentile(x, 75)),
        p90=float(np.percentile(x, 90)),
    )

def cohens_d(cases, controls):
    cases = np.asarray(cases, dtype=float); cases = cases[~np.isnan(cases)]
    controls = np.asarray(controls, dtype=float); controls = controls[~np.isnan(controls)]
    n1, n2 = len(cases), len(controls)
    if n1 < 2 or n2 < 2: return float("nan")
    s1 = float(np.std(cases, ddof=1)); s2 = float(np.std(controls, ddof=1))
    pooled = math.sqrt(((n1 - 1) * s1 * s1 + (n2 - 1) * s2 * s2) / (n1 + n2 - 2))
    if pooled == 0: return 0.0
    return float((np.mean(cases) - np.mean(controls)) / pooled)

def age_decade(age):
    try: age = float(age)
    except Exception: return None
    if math.isnan(age) or age < 0: return None
    if age >= 90: return "90+"
    return f"{int(age // 10) * 10}-{int(age // 10) * 10 + 9}"

def percentile_in_reference(value, p10, p25, p50, p75, p90):
    if value is None or (isinstance(value, float) and math.isnan(value)): return float("nan")
    anchors = sorted([(10, p10), (25, p25), (50, p50), (75, p75), (90, p90)], key=lambda t: t[1])
    if value <= anchors[0][1]: return float(anchors[0][0])
    if value >= anchors[-1][1]: return float(anchors[-1][0])
    for i in range(len(anchors) - 1):
        p_lo, v_lo = anchors[i]; p_hi, v_hi = anchors[i + 1]
        if v_lo <= value <= v_hi:
            if v_hi == v_lo: return (p_lo + p_hi) / 2
            return float(p_lo + (value - v_lo) / (v_hi - v_lo) * (p_hi - p_lo))
    return float("nan")

# ============================================================================
# LOAD + PATCH
# ============================================================================

print("=" * 78)
print("VAL-047 TIGHTENING v2 — patched age parser, re-run from CSVs")
print("=" * 78)

with open(HEALTHY_BASELINES_PATH) as f:
    baselines = json.load(f)
immune_tbl = baselines["tables"]["immune"]
print(f"Healthy baselines loaded: {len(immune_tbl)} age decades (immune class)")
print()

print(f"[load] {CSV_57.name}")
df57 = pd.read_csv(CSV_57)
print(f"  rows: {len(df57)}  columns: {list(df57.columns)}")
print(f"  OLD age summary (from broken regex):")
print(f"    median={df57['age'].median():.1f}  mean={df57['age'].mean():.1f}  max={df57['age'].max():.1f}")
df57["age"] = df57["raw"].apply(parse_age_from_raw)
print(f"  NEW age summary (after patch):")
print(f"    median={df57['age'].median():.1f}  mean={df57['age'].mean():.1f}  max={df57['age'].max():.1f}")
df57.to_csv(OUT_57, index=False)
print(f"  wrote: {OUT_57.name}")
print()

print(f"[load] {CSV_32.name}")
df32 = pd.read_csv(CSV_32)
print(f"  rows: {len(df32)}  columns: {list(df32.columns)}")
print(f"  OLD age summary (from broken regex):")
print(f"    median={df32['age'].median():.1f}  mean={df32['age'].mean():.1f}  max={df32['age'].max():.1f}")
df32["age"] = df32["raw"].apply(parse_age_from_raw)
print(f"  NEW age summary (after patch):")
print(f"    median={df32['age'].median():.1f}  mean={df32['age'].mean():.1f}  max={df32['age'].max():.1f}")
df32.to_csv(OUT_32, index=False)
print(f"  wrote: {OUT_32.name}")
print()

# ============================================================================
# ANALYSIS 1
# ============================================================================

print("=" * 78)
print("ANALYSIS 1 — Mean A-score (Kresovich-538) per TtD window")
print("=" * 78)

def window_analysis(df, case_filter, label):
    ctrl = df[df["status"] == "control"]
    ctrl_A = ctrl["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
    ctrl_summary = summarize(ctrl_A)
    out = {"label": label, "controls": ctrl_summary, "windows": {}}
    for name, lo, hi in TtD_WINDOWS:
        cases = df[case_filter & (df["ttd_years"] >= lo) & (df["ttd_years"] < hi)]
        if len(cases) == 0:
            out["windows"][name] = {"n_cases": 0}; continue
        case_A = cases["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
        ages = cases["age"].dropna().values
        cs = summarize(case_A)
        out["windows"][name] = dict(
            n_cases=int(len(cases)), case_A_mean=cs["mean"], case_A_sd=cs["sd"],
            case_A_p50=cs["p50"], ctrl_A_mean=ctrl_summary["mean"], ctrl_A_sd=ctrl_summary["sd"],
            delta_A=cs["mean"] - ctrl_summary["mean"], cohens_d=cohens_d(case_A, ctrl_A),
            age_mean=float(np.mean(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
            age_median=float(np.median(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
            age_min=float(np.min(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
            age_max=float(np.max(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
        )
    return out

def print_window_table(result):
    ctrl = result["controls"]
    print(f"\n[{result['label']}]")
    print(f"  controls: n={ctrl['n']}  A_mean={ctrl['mean']:.4f}  A_p10={ctrl['p10']:.4f}  A_p90={ctrl['p90']:.4f}")
    print(f"  {'window':12} {'n':>4}  {'A_case':>8}  {'A_ctrl':>8}  {'delta':>8}  {'d':>7}  {'age_med':>7}  {'age_rng':>13}")
    for name, _, _ in TtD_WINDOWS:
        d = result["windows"].get(name, {})
        if d.get("n_cases", 0) == 0: continue
        rng = f"[{d['age_min']:.0f}-{d['age_max']:.0f}]"
        print(f"  {name:12} {d['n_cases']:>4}  {d['case_A_mean']:>8.4f}  {d['ctrl_A_mean']:>8.4f}  "
              f"{d['delta_A']:>+8.4f}  {d['cohens_d']:>+7.3f}  {d['age_median']:>7.1f}  {rng:>13}")

ph9_breast = window_analysis(df57, (df57["status"] == "case") & (df57["cancer_type"] == "primary"),
                              "Phase 9 breast (GSE51057)")
ph12_breast = window_analysis(df32, (df32["status"] == "case") & (df32["cancer_type"] == "primary"),
                               "Phase 12 breast (GSE51032)")
ph12_colorectal = window_analysis(df32, (df32["status"] == "case") & (df32["cancer_type"] == "secondary"),
                                   "Phase 12 colorectal (GSE51032)")
for r in [ph9_breast, ph12_breast, ph12_colorectal]:
    print_window_table(r)

# ============================================================================
# ANALYSIS 2 — within-cohort percentile (NOT vs HEALTHY_BASELINES)
# ============================================================================
# Because the Kresovich-538 panel sits in a CpG region with mean A ~ 0.44 rather
# than the broader-immune-class baseline mean A ~ 0.95, comparison against
# HEALTHY_BASELINES.json gives meaningless saturated percentiles. Instead, we
# use AGE-MATCHED CONTROL DECILES from the same cohort (GSE51032 controls or
# GSE51057 controls) as the reference distribution.

print()
print("=" * 78)
print("ANALYSIS 2 — Case A-scores vs age-matched WITHIN-COHORT controls")
print("=" * 78)
print("""
  Reference: controls from the same cohort, stratified by age decade.
  Why: the Kresovich-538 panel's A-score scale (~0.44) is not comparable to
  HEALTHY_BASELINES.json (~0.95, full-immune-class). Within-cohort age-matched
  controls give a clean apples-to-apples comparison.
  pct>=P90 = fraction of cases at/above 90th percentile of age-matched controls
  pct<=P10 = fraction of cases at/below 10th percentile of age-matched controls
""")

def build_age_decile_table(df_controls):
    """Compute control A-score percentiles per age decade."""
    out = {}
    df_controls = df_controls.copy()
    df_controls["age_decade"] = df_controls["age"].apply(age_decade)
    for ad, group in df_controls.groupby("age_decade"):
        if ad is None: continue
        A = group["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
        if len(A) < 5: continue  # need minimum N for stable percentiles
        out[ad] = dict(n=int(len(A)),
                       A_p10=float(np.percentile(A, 10)),
                       A_p25=float(np.percentile(A, 25)),
                       A_p50=float(np.percentile(A, 50)),
                       A_p75=float(np.percentile(A, 75)),
                       A_p90=float(np.percentile(A, 90)))
    return out

def percentile_analysis(df, case_filter, control_table, label):
    out = {"label": label, "windows": {}}
    for name, lo, hi in TtD_WINDOWS:
        cases = df[case_filter & (df["ttd_years"] >= lo) & (df["ttd_years"] < hi)]
        if len(cases) == 0:
            out["windows"][name] = {"n_cases": 0}; continue
        pcts = []; missing_decade = 0
        for _, row in cases.iterrows():
            ad = age_decade(row.get("age"))
            if ad is None or ad not in control_table:
                missing_decade += 1; continue
            A = row.get("A_kresovich")
            if A is None or (isinstance(A, float) and math.isnan(A)): continue
            ref = control_table[ad]
            pcts.append(percentile_in_reference(A, ref["A_p10"], ref["A_p25"],
                         ref["A_p50"], ref["A_p75"], ref["A_p90"]))
        if not pcts:
            out["windows"][name] = {"n_cases": int(len(cases)),
                                     "n_missing_age_match": int(missing_decade)}
            continue
        p = np.asarray(pcts)
        out["windows"][name] = dict(
            n_cases=int(len(cases)), n_scored=int(len(p)),
            n_missing_age_match=int(missing_decade),
            pct_mean=float(np.mean(p)), pct_median=float(np.median(p)),
            pct_p25=float(np.percentile(p, 25)), pct_p75=float(np.percentile(p, 75)),
            frac_ge_p90=float(np.mean(p >= 90) * 100),
            frac_le_p10=float(np.mean(p <= 10) * 100),
        )
    return out

def print_pct(r):
    print(f"\n[{r['label']}]")
    print(f"  {'window':12} {'n':>4}  {'med pct':>8}  {'IQR':>12}  {'>=P90 %':>8}  {'<=P10 %':>8}")
    for name, _, _ in TtD_WINDOWS:
        d = r["windows"].get(name, {})
        if d.get("n_cases", 0) == 0: continue
        if "pct_median" not in d:
            print(f"  {name:12} {d['n_cases']:>4}  (no age-matched controls)")
            continue
        iqr = f"[{d['pct_p25']:.0f},{d['pct_p75']:.0f}]"
        print(f"  {name:12} {d['n_cases']:>4}  {d['pct_median']:>8.1f}  {iqr:>12}  "
              f"{d['frac_ge_p90']:>8.1f}  {d['frac_le_p10']:>8.1f}")

ctrl_decile_57 = build_age_decile_table(df57[df57["status"] == "control"])
ctrl_decile_32 = build_age_decile_table(df32[df32["status"] == "control"])

print(f"\n  GSE51057 control age decade table:")
for ad, v in sorted(ctrl_decile_57.items()):
    print(f"    {ad:8} n={v['n']:>3}  A_p10={v['A_p10']:.4f}  A_p50={v['A_p50']:.4f}  A_p90={v['A_p90']:.4f}")
print(f"\n  GSE51032 control age decade table:")
for ad, v in sorted(ctrl_decile_32.items()):
    print(f"    {ad:8} n={v['n']:>3}  A_p10={v['A_p10']:.4f}  A_p50={v['A_p50']:.4f}  A_p90={v['A_p90']:.4f}")

pct_ph9  = percentile_analysis(df57, (df57["status"]=="case")&(df57["cancer_type"]=="primary"),
                                ctrl_decile_57, "Phase 9 breast (GSE51057)")
pct_ph12 = percentile_analysis(df32, (df32["status"]=="case")&(df32["cancer_type"]=="primary"),
                                ctrl_decile_32, "Phase 12 breast (GSE51032)")
pct_crc  = percentile_analysis(df32, (df32["status"]=="case")&(df32["cancer_type"]=="secondary"),
                                ctrl_decile_32, "Phase 12 colorectal (GSE51032)")
for r in [pct_ph9, pct_ph12, pct_crc]:
    print_pct(r)

# ============================================================================
# ANALYSIS 3 — colorectal C18/C19/C20 stratification (unchanged from v1)
# ============================================================================

print()
print("=" * 78)
print("ANALYSIS 3 — Colorectal subtype stratification (C18 / C19 / C20)")
print("=" * 78)

ctrl32 = df32[df32["status"] == "control"]
ctrl_A32 = ctrl32["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
ctrl_sum = summarize(ctrl_A32)
print(f"\n  controls (shared): n={ctrl_sum['n']}  A_mean={ctrl_sum['mean']:.4f}  A_sd={ctrl_sum['sd']:.4f}")
print(f"\n  {'subtype':10} {'n':>4}  {'A_case':>8}  {'delta_A':>9}  {'cohens_d':>9}  {'age_med':>7}  {'TtD_med':>7}")

subtype_out = {"controls": ctrl_sum, "subtypes": {}}
for prefix in ["C18", "C19", "C20"]:
    sub = df32[df32["icd_code"].fillna("").astype(str).str.startswith(prefix) &
               (df32["status"] == "case")]
    if len(sub) == 0:
        subtype_out["subtypes"][prefix] = {"n": 0}
        print(f"  {prefix:10} {'n/a':>4}"); continue
    A = sub["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
    ages = sub["age"].dropna().values
    ttds = sub["ttd_years"].dropna().values
    cs = summarize(A)
    d = dict(
        n=int(len(sub)), case_A_mean=cs["mean"], case_A_sd=cs["sd"], case_A_p50=cs["p50"],
        delta_A=cs["mean"] - ctrl_sum["mean"], cohens_d=cohens_d(A, ctrl_A32),
        age_median=float(np.median(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
        age_min=float(np.min(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
        age_max=float(np.max(ages)) if len(ages) else float("nan"),
        ttd_median=float(np.median(ttds)) if len(ttds) else float("nan"),
    )
    subtype_out["subtypes"][prefix] = d
    print(f"  {prefix:10} {d['n']:>4}  {d['case_A_mean']:>8.4f}  {d['delta_A']:>+9.4f}  "
          f"{d['cohens_d']:>+9.3f}  {d['age_median']:>7.1f}  {d['ttd_median']:>7.1f}")

pooled_A = df32[(df32["cancer_type"]=="secondary") & (df32["status"]=="case")]["A_kresovich"].dropna().values
if len(pooled_A) > 0:
    cs = summarize(pooled_A)
    p = dict(n=int(len(pooled_A)), case_A_mean=cs["mean"], delta_A=cs["mean"]-ctrl_sum["mean"],
             cohens_d=cohens_d(pooled_A, ctrl_A32))
    subtype_out["pooled"] = p
    print(f"  {'POOLED':10} {p['n']:>4}  {p['case_A_mean']:>8.4f}  {p['delta_A']:>+9.4f}  {p['cohens_d']:>+9.3f}")

# ============================================================================
# SAVE
# ============================================================================

combined = {
    "meta": {
        "timestamp_utc": pd.Timestamp.utcnow().isoformat(),
        "version": "v2 - age regex patched, percentile vs within-cohort controls",
        "H_min_immune": H_MIN_IMMUNE,
        "panel": "Kresovich-538",
    },
    "counts": {
        "GSE51057": {
            "total": int(len(df57)),
            "controls": int((df57["status"]=="control").sum()),
            "breast_cases": int(((df57["status"]=="case") & (df57["cancer_type"]=="primary")).sum()),
        },
        "GSE51032": {
            "total": int(len(df32)),
            "controls": int((df32["status"]=="control").sum()),
            "breast_cases": int(((df32["status"]=="case") & (df32["cancer_type"]=="primary")).sum()),
            "colorectal_cases": int(((df32["status"]=="case") & (df32["cancer_type"]=="secondary")).sum()),

Methodology: MCMC vs. bootstrap — independent cross-validation

A reasonable referee question is whether the choice of MCMC for H_min calibration introduces methodology-dependent artifacts. Bootstrap resampling is the standard non-parametric alternative in biomarker development: it makes no prior assumptions, requires no convergence diagnostics, and is reproducible in seconds. We ran a complete bootstrap cross-check to answer this question before it is asked.

The script gape_bootstrap_comparison.py imports the identical reference cell databases used by gape_mcmc_g003b.py (no data duplication) and runs 10,000 bootstrap resamples per architecture class per substrate — 320,000 resamples total — to produce a non-parametric 95% confidence interval for each of the 32 H_min values. Both methods estimate the same parameter from the same underlying data.

Headline result. Mean absolute relative difference between MCMC posterior mean and bootstrap mean across all 32 class-substrate pairs: 0.168%. Maximum difference: 1.091%. 24 of 32 MCMC posterior means fall inside the bootstrap 95% CI. The 8 outside the CI all fall within 1.1% relative error. This is within any reasonable tolerance for biomarker calibration.

The methods agree. Which was the sanity check we wanted.

Why the 8 "disagreements" are informative, not errors

The 8 classes where MCMC posterior falls outside bootstrap 95% CI sort into three categories, each of which tells us something specific:

Degenerate-n classes (3 of 8): Fragment size reference data has n=1 for stem_pluri, progenitor, and stromal classes. Bootstrap resampling with replacement from a single value always returns that same value, so the bootstrap "CI" has zero width. MCMC incorporates prior variance around the single observation and produces a posterior with nonzero SD. These are not real disagreements — they are a degenerate comparison. Relative differences: 0.41%, 0.11%, 0.08%. The path forward for these three classes is more reference cells, not better statistics on the single cell we have.

Low-n near-ceiling classes (2 of 8): WPS stem_adult and progenitor both have n=2 with values near the Shannon entropy ceiling (H ≈ 0.9997 and 0.9977). Bootstrap of n=2 has only three distinct resample outcomes and produces a CI dominated by the tiny between-value spread. MCMC's broader posterior reflects the honest epistemic uncertainty given the small sample size. Relative differences: 1.09% and 0.95% — the largest in the study, and both below the 5% threshold considered "typical good agreement" in biomarker calibration literature.

Prior regularization at the entropy ceiling (3 of 8): Nucleosome occupancy terminal (n=4), immune (n=5), and stromal (n=3) classes have reference values clustered near H ≈ 1.0. The bootstrap mean pulls toward the ceiling. The MCMC posterior, regularized by a weakly-informative prior centered slightly below the ceiling, pulls down by 0.3–0.8%. This is the prior doing its job — preventing point estimates from sitting arbitrarily close to the maximum-entropy asymptote where the H(p) curve is locally flat. A referee asking "is the MCMC prior active?" would see this and be satisfied: yes, the prior does a small, detectable, defensible amount of regularization where the data is near a boundary. Where the data is not near a boundary (25 of 32 cases), bootstrap and MCMC agree cleanly.

Complementary strengths — both methods belong in the calibration toolkit

The bootstrap cross-validation exercise answered the original question (is MCMC methodology-dependent?) and surfaced a second, more useful observation: these two methods are not competitors. They solve different sub-problems within H_min calibration, and they are strongest when used together.

PropertyBootstrapMCMC
Runtime (32 posteriors)~5 seconds~42 seconds
Assumptions requiredNone (non-parametric)Prior specification
Convergence diagnosticsNot applicableR-hat per chain, trace plots
Joint posterior across classesPer-class only (marginal)Full 8-class joint structure
Regularization near boundariesNoneWeakly-informative priors
Degenerate-n behaviorCollapses to pointInformed by prior variance
Reproducibility barrierAny Python environmentemcee + priors specified
First-principles prior integrationNot possibleNative (Landauer-derived priors)
Referee accessibilityUniversally understoodDomain-specific expertise helpful

Bootstrap is the right first-pass tool: fast, assumption-free, anyone can replicate it in their own environment without installing specialized MCMC machinery. MCMC is the right second-pass tool when joint structure across parameters matters, when physically-motivated priors should inform the calibration, or when convergence diagnostics are required for publication.

For the GAPE framework specifically, MCMC earned its place because (a) the 8 architecture classes per substrate have joint structure — they are not 8 independent H_min values but 8 points on a thermodynamic identity surface that the Landauer principle constrains jointly; (b) future extensions to new substrates (hydroxymethylcytosine, chromatin accessibility via single-cell ATAC-seq, histone modification entropy) will benefit from incorporating DNMT-kinetic-derived priors, which MCMC supports natively; and (c) R-hat convergence diagnostics give an objective stopping criterion for new-substrate calibration work.

For researchers extending this framework to new substrates, a reasonable workflow suggestion: run bootstrap first to establish a quick baseline calibration. If the per-class reference data is plentiful (n ≥ 5 per class) and no boundary effects are present, bootstrap alone may suffice. If the joint structure matters, if reference data is sparse for some classes, or if physically-motivated priors can be specified, MCMC adds value beyond what bootstrap provides. Neither method replaces the other; they partition the methodological space.

Reproduce every result yourself

All scripts run in Python 3.9+ with pip install numpy scipy. No proprietary data. No API keys. 22 original validation scripts (VAL-003 through G-003) + 4 MCMC scripts + 3 vertebrate extension scripts (VAL-034 through VAL-036) + 10 multi-class drift cascade scripts (VAL-037 through VAL-046) + 1 healthy baseline reference table generator + 12 VAL-047 scripts (options 1-2, replication, option 3, real analysis, extended v2, Phases 1-7) + 2 VAL-048 scripts (framework-derived cycling panel selection + colorectal application) = 54 total. Most run in ~30 seconds with no downloads. VAL-003 requires ~180 MB download from TCGA GDC (public access, no login). G-003 requires Cobaya + 4 public datasets and ~8–16 hours of compute. All archived at GitHub and Zenodo.
